title: Raise cache capacity and lower random-read cost to cut GetUserTweets terminal occupancy
configuration_cause: shared_buffers=16384 (128MB) is far below the 2TB host memory; effective_cache_size=524288 (4GB) undervalues cache; effective_io_concurrency=1 and random_page_cost=4.0 make the planner overprice cached random index reads, so GetUserTweets (88.5% of terminal capacity, p95 410us) pays physical DataFileRead latency.
mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.885) with p95 410us while wait samples show DataFileRead (35) and BufferIO (6) and telemetry flags low_buffer_hit_ratio. A 128MB shared_buffers cannot retain the tweets working set, and random_page_cost=4.0 with effective_io_concurrency=1 makes index paths look expensive. Enlarging shared_buffers to 1GB, raising effective_cache_size to 12GB, enabling prefetch concurrency, and lowering random_page_cost to 1.5 while keeping seq_page_cost=1.0 should convert physical reads into buffer hits, shrinking per-transaction service time and freeing terminal capacity for more completed transactions.
query_effect: Index scans on tweets should be costed as mostly cached; fewer physical DataFileRead stalls per GetUserTweets call.
expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps above 20596 as GetUserTweets service time falls.
expected_latency_effect: Decrease GetUserTweets p95 and overall p95.

predictions.rationale: Larger buffer pool plus cheaper random-read costing reduces physical reads on the dominant index path.
Shorter GetUserTweets service time frees terminal capacity.
More cached pages reduce IO waiters.
Lower per-transaction service time raises completed throughput.

alternatives.statement: If the gain is instead WAL-bound, WALSync wait and wal_waiting_backends would move while buffer metrics stay flat; that is the memory_storage WAL bundle, not this action.
If only planner costing matters, plan_changed would appear without io_waiting_backends reduction; here we predict both move together.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves 128MB shared_buffers and pessimistic random_page_cost on a 2TB host while the dominant transaction is index-scan bound with observed DataFileRead waits; the coherent cache bundle directly targets that bottleneck.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 1GB = 131072*8kB, 8x current, well inside 8192-65536? no: exceeds high 65536, so use 65536 (512MB)

knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost

nodes.label: cached index reads reduce physical IO

cross_domain_requirements: WAL bundle (wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay, wal_compression) is memory_storage scope; not executed here.
